AGENDA

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings. This meeting will be held via videoconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19 and pursuant to the Governor's Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer's Safer at Home Order (revised March 21, 2020). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.
HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. The meeting will not be livestreamed. You may attend the meeting through a computer or telephone:
BY COMPUTER:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/85393253003
Zoom Meeting ID: 853 9325 3003 or
BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code 853 9325 3003#
HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit email correspondence to CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org before the meeting begins. The email will be distributed to all councilmembers. Public correspondence submitted electronically via email will be provided to the legislative body, but will not be read aloud at the meeting.
HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: If you would like to address the City Council during the meeting, please email CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org by 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, July 14th, with (1) your name, (2) the agenda item on which you'd like to speak, and (3) the phone number and/or Zoom name from which you will be calling in to the meeting.

MINUTES
  OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

A Teleconference meeting of the Palos Verdes Estates City Council meeting via Zoom pursuant to
Executive Order N25-20 issued by Governor Gavin Newsom on March 26, 2020, was called to order
by Mayor McGowan at 6:32 P.M. on July 14, 2020, notice having been given with affidavit thereto
on file. Members of the public were provided with the following information to provide public
input:
  BY COMPUTER:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/85393253003

  Zoom Meeting ID: 853 9325 3003 or

  BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code 853 9325 3003#

Karen Logan, and Joan Davidson.

CEREMONIAL MATTERS - None

PUBLIC HEARING(S)

8.  Resolution No. R20-23 Estates Adopting a Comprehensive Fee Schedule Establishing
  and Amending Certain Service and Development-Related Fees for City Services

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kao, Seconded by Councilmember Davidson to
  approve Resolution No. R20-23 adopting a comprehensive fee schedule establishing and
  amending certain service and development related fees for city services, with the following
  amendments: that the Parklands Committee fee for trimming City trees be waived; that a resident
  need not apply for residential tree trimming permit for the same tree more than once in a 5-year
  period; and that the ADU permit fee be revisited in a September meeting. The motion
  carried by the following roll call vote:

  AYES:  Lozzi, Kao, Davidson, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES:  None

9.  PC-534-20; Appeal of May 14, 2020 Parklands Committee Recommendation for an
  Application to Remove One Italian Stone Pine Tree Located Adjacent To 1332 Via
  Gabriel

  The following individuals addressed the City Council: Kathleen Andersson, Jeffrey Nolan,
  and Emily Deruyter. The Appellant Alan Haven also addressed the City Council.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kao, Seconded by Councilmember Davidson to
  deny the present appeal and affirm the decision of the Parklands Committee, by Resolution R20-

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
July 14, 2020
   24, to deny Mr. Haven’s application for a permit to remove the Italian Stone Pine tree located in the
  parkway adjacent to 1332 Via Gabriel. The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  AYES:  Lozzi, Kao, Davidson, McGowan
  NOES:  Kemps

OLD BUSINESS
None

NEW BUSINESS

10.  School Resource Officer Program

  The following individuals addressed the City Council: Dr. Alex Cherniss, Rick Phillips, and
  Desiree Myers

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Kemps for the City not to approve or authorize the
  Mayor to sign the First Amendment to Memorandum of Understanding with the other
  Peninsula cities and the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District to fund the School
  Resource Officer Program. The motion died for lack of second.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Davidson, Seconded by Councilmember Kao to
  approve and authorize the Mayor to sign the First Amendment to Memorandum of
  Understanding with the other Peninsula cities and the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School
  District to fund the School Resource Officer Program. The motion carried by the following
  roll call vote:

  AYES:  Lozzi, Kao, Davidson, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES:  Kemps

11.  Palos Verdes Golf Club Request for a Permanent Transfer of Funds from their Club
  Improvement Account to their Operating Account

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Kemps, Seconded by Councilmember Lozzi to
  approve the Palos Verdes Golf Club’s request for permanent relief from paying the current
  inter-fund balance of $400,000 due from the Operations Fund to the Club Improvement Fund
  (CIF); and a permanent $312,626 inter-fund transfer from the CIF to the Operations Fund, for
  a total of $712,626, and waive the associated 10% fee associated with the transfer. The motion
  carried by the following roll call vote:

  AYES:  Lozzi, Kao, Davidson, Kemps
  NOES:  McGowan

STAFF REPORTS

  i.  City Manager's Report
  City Manager Guglielmo reported on the interim City Engineer, updated City Hall
  protocols, the gas leaf-blower ordinance and traffic enforcement,
  a. State of the Police Department

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
July 14, 2020
   Interim Police Chief Dreiling provided information about enforcement for the leaf blower
  ordinance.

MAYOR & CITY COUNCILMEMBERS' REPORTS

Councilmember Lozzi – Requested future Pension ad-hoc action items

Councilmember Davidson – Discussed the garden at Mirlo Gate Tower, a Grant writer and requested
a future agenda item to discuss term limits. Thanked City Manager Guglielmo and noted the
celebration of Bastille Day.

Councilmember Kao – Provided an update on actions and legislative positions of the South Bay Cities
Council of Governments.

Mayor Pro Tem Kemps – requested Pension ad-hoc presentation in September, requested that staff
proceed with referrals or proposals for audio/video in City Hall, requested the City implement Mind
Cast for emails, requested future agenda items for transparency including: restricting use of side-letter
agreements, review municipal code items for purchasing, scanning City documents and making them
accessible, and increasing transparency on the website.

Mayor McGowan – reported on the Golf and Tennis Club task force to generate additional revenue.
